points.title: Real shared extraction
points.description: The resource-delta recipe is used by two different production packs (ordered parade and resource-track race). Specific mechanics stay outside the runtime.

points.title: Catalogue matrix
points.description: All 39 games and 38 packs are mapped across 14 categories. Every positive cell links to source lines. Empty cells explicitly mean no direct static evidence, not absence of a capability.

points.title: Composable conditions
points.description: Existing all/any/not, ownership, position, resources and statuses are extended with phase-is and bounded numeric comparison.

points.title: Common selectors
points.description: Current player and predicate-selected participants join existing self/opponents/next/previous. Owners and occupants use predicates over canonical controllers.

points.title: Bounded expressions
points.description: Thirteen expression variants cover constants, canonical reads, arithmetic, min/max and clamp. Hand/inventory/player counts use their canonical controllers.

points.title: Closed deterministic DSL
points.description: Schema validation rejects functions, arbitrary property access and unknown instructions. Expressions and triggers have depth/node/execution budgets; division by zero and unsafe results fail.

points.title: Configurable resources
points.description: resource.pool declares initial/min/max independently of resource identity. Balances remain solely in playerValues.resources; declared bounds apply to mutation and restoration.

points.title: Payment workflow
points.description: quoteResourcePayment computes affordability and settlement before mutation. Controller operations share the same calculation; elimination remains a match decision.

points.title: Insufficient funds policies
points.description: Explicit cancel, debt, partial and eliminate policies are supported. Existing allowPartial and default rejection retain their semantics. Explicit resource bounds cannot be bypassed by debt.

points.title: Status lifecycle
points.description: Status buckets identify targets canonically. Optional source, charges, categories and parameters join duration and expiry. Charge consumption is independent of turn expiry.

points.title: Generic protections
points.description: Effect categories are intercepted before mutation. Exact effect kinds and movement/resource/card/inventory loss categories consume one matching protection charge.

points.title: Movement and consequences
points.description: The existing movement controller owns displacement and emits events. Landing/pass recipes and the new event triggers compose consequences separately.

points.title: Movement configuration
points.description: Track overshoot supports clamp/wrap/bounce/exact; signed moves, teleport, blocked landing pipelines and pawn/grid capabilities preserve their specialized topology contracts.

points.title: Collision detection and resolution
points.description: Detection uses canonical positions/occupants; effects resolve independently through selectors and displacement or ownership operations. No game-specific collision policy enters the core.

points.title: Card locations
points.description: Deck, hand, discard and named zones are canonical locations. Market/removed areas are ordinary public/private zones. moveCard validates both endpoints before mutating one occurrence.

points.title: Card operations
points.description: Existing draw, transfer, discard, zone visibility, shuffle and selection controllers remain common. move-card adds JSON/API movement between all location kinds without duplicating card storage.

points.title: Shared interactions
points.description: Existing choice/submission/vote controllers define participants, options, private answers, validation and completion. Domain recipes compose these capabilities rather than storing alternate interaction state.

points.title: Collections
points.description: Existing set completion and request-card recipes operate on canonical hands. Completion moves cards once and derived collection views read the resulting state.

points.title: Ownership semantics
points.description: Registry assets use the shared ownership controller. Card possession is canonical in card locations and inventory possession in inventory buckets; no parallel ownership registry is introduced for either.

points.title: Declarative triggers
points.description: Patterns declare action or event triggers with scalar event filters. Existing movement/turn/resource/card events feed the same bounded dispatcher. Trigger effects cannot suspend for an interactive choice.

points.title: Composition pipeline
points.description: Triggers dispatch conditions, target selectors and numeric expressions into existing effect primitives. JSON and TypeScript builders share the same compiled trigger definitions.

points.title: Composable victory
points.description: conditionVictory evaluates local predicates per participant, with all/any/not composition and explicit tie policy. Existing score/resource/position/collection predicates need no custom callback.

points.title: Recipes outside core
points.description: resourceDeltaEffects lives above the runtime and composes public instructions. Two production packs consume it while keeping their reward/tile policies.

points.title: Specific packs remain specific
points.description: All 38 packs remain classified as specific. No promotion is claimed merely because a pack has configuration. Common recipe extraction does not reverse dependency direction.

points.title: Responsibility splitting
points.description: Common resource-delta loops leave two packs; resource and card-location responsibilities have dedicated controllers. Existing pack size and production/behavior line budgets remain unchanged.

points.title: Evidence-based reuse governance
points.description: Promotion gates require independent consumers and an ADR. The new recipe has a test locating actual calls from two catalogue games.

points.title: Dependency direction
points.description: Existing AST import and dependency-cycle checks protect runtime/rules/core direction. Trigger validation is separate from pattern construction to avoid a runtime cycle.

points.title: Public facades
points.description: Authors and extensions use their explicit facades. New contracts and builders are exported intentionally; pack imports remain checked against deep runtime access.

points.title: Versioned author API
points.description: Author/public API is 10.0.0. Transitive declarations are snapshotted; amount unions and new exhaustive variants are documented as a major migration.

points.title: Versioned extension API
points.description: Extension API/contracts are 2.0.0, including the widened amount and component contracts. Four independently checked snapshots cover all facades.

points.title: JSON/API parity
points.description: Exhaustive primitive cases include new expressions, selectors, payments, protections and card movement. Assertions compare engine state, events and deterministic replay; trigger parity uses three seeds.

points.title: Closed core JSON
points.description: New behavior enters closed component/pattern/condition/effect variants. No game-business root fields or arbitrary state-path expressions are added.

points.title: Controlled vocabulary
points.description: Existing semantic conditions compose owners/occupants and victory rules. New variants represent reusable capabilities; market and removed zones need no dedicated business keywords.

points.title: Structured diagnostics
points.description: Author schemas and reference validators retain path/origin diagnostics. SDK effect sequences now pass closed schema validation before typed semantic validation.

points.title: Validated type boundaries
points.description: The effect validator no longer asserts an unknown object to GameEffectInstruction. It uses the asserting closed schema codec. Existing double-cast lint and facade rules remain enforced.

points.title: Schema/type CI contracts
points.description: New schemas satisfy AuthorSchema, and exhaustive cases cover new discriminated unions. Typecheck, schema tests and merge-contract tests remain in the required workflow.

points.title: Formal state ownership
points.description: Ownership declarations now include resource pools and canonical player values. Restoration validates resource bounds and status metadata rather than inferring fields.

points.title: Canonical storage
points.description: Expressions, selectors and cards read/write controller-owned state. Resource pools retain only static bounds in definitions. No second score, hand, inventory or position map is introduced.

points.title: Static content isolation
points.description: Existing immutable content and setup isolation contracts remain. New resource/trigger definitions are compiled as static definitions, while session state contains only mutable values.

points.title: Deterministic execution
points.description: Expressions are pure canonical reads. Triggers use deterministic order and bounded dispatch. Replay corpus compares live, replayed and restored state for identical seeds/commands/version.

points.title: Injected RNG
points.description: Existing seeded RNG is the only randomness source for rules. Numeric expressions and selectors add no system randomness; generated actions and reference replays exercise seeded choices.

points.title: All catalogue replays
points.description: Every one of the 39 games runs a bounded command campaign. The six historical references are retained, and all additional references are checked without snapshot update.

points.title: Multiple seeds
points.description: Each game runs seeds 11, 23 and 67, plus historical non-overlapping seed cases: 120 references. A legitimate event burst exposed the 128-event buffer limit; it is now bounded at 512 and overflow remains tested.

points.title: Generated invariant models
points.description: Existing generated movement/resource/RNG and card/inventory/ownership campaigns are retained. Payment tests add exhaustive independent balance/cost/policy models, and expression/trigger tests cover invalid and cyclic effects.

validation.mergeGate: Full integration and release-artifact certification must succeed on the final PR head before merging.
validation.followup: Full local campaign: 275 suites passed, two diagnostic regressions found and corrected; all 120 snapshots passed. Rerun of both failed suites and four related suites: 389 tests passed. Both regressions are now part of engine:merge-contracts. Restored status metadata shape guards: five malformed-save cases added; 232 status/invariant/parity tests passed.
